product_family: AI agent / workflow automation platform for operations and finance teams (Parabola "Flows" builder plus AI-powered steps); single core product with a self-serve tier and an Enterprise tier (SSO/SAML, dedicated automation-engineer implementation, role-based access). Not to be confused with the unrelated product "Parabol" (parabol.co), a meeting-notes tool.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: "SOC2 Compliant" badge (image labeled "SOC 2 type II badge"); elsewhere on the vendor's own site: "Parabola is SOC 2 compliant" and the Enterprise page lists "SOC 2 Type II" as an included capability.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on parabola.io. The security page, security FAQs, shared-data-responsibility page, and privacy policy make no mention of ISO 27001. (A third-party aggregator, nudgesecurity.com, lists Parabola as "ISO 27001 Compliant" but this is not a vendor-domain source and could not be corroborated on parabola.io.)

certifications.name: GDPR (posture / DPA)
certifications.proof_quote: "Parabola offers a Data Protection Agreement as a means of meeting the adequacy and security requirements of the European Parliament and Council of the European Union's Data Protection Directive and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)." The DPA itself: "AES 256-bit encryption for Customer Data stored in Parabola's production environment" and commits to a maintained subprocessor list with 14 days' notice of changes.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: "Customer acknowledges that the Services are not intended to meet any legal obligations for these uses, including HIPAA requirements, and that Parabola is not a Business Associate as defined under HIPAA." Protected health information is explicitly listed as "Prohibited Data."

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: "All payments made to Parabola go through our payment processing partner, Stripe." Payment-card data is listed as "Prohibited Data" for use within the product itself ("credit, debit or other payment card data subject to the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS)..."); any PCI compliance is Stripe's, not Parabola's own certification.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on parabola.io; FedRAMP is not mentioned on the security page, security FAQs, or legal pages. A third-party aggregator (nudgesecurity.com) claims 'FedRamp Compliant,' but this is not corroborated on the vendor's own domain.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on parabola.io. (Third-party aggregator nudgesecurity.com claims "CSA Star Level 1 Compliant" but this is not corroborated on the vendor's own domain.)

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI Governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an AI-governance certification on the vendor's own domain.

certifications.name: CSA STAR AI
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of CSA STAR AI on the vendor's own domain.

privacy.ai_training_note: Vendor documentation states Parabola does not train its own AI models on customer data, and that its third-party LLM providers are used under enterprise agreements: "Parabola maintains enterprise-level agreements with its third-party AI model providers (incl. OpenAI and Anthropic) that include Data Processing Agreements" which "contractually prohibit the providers from using the contents of any data sent through Parabola's AI steps as training data for their models." No opt-out toggle or tier distinction is described in the available documentation; the posture is stated as a blanket contractual guarantee rather than a per-account opt-out control, which is a minor gap in transparency for enterprise buyers who want to self-verify.
privacy.data_region: US-hosted (AWS, servers in the United States); EU/Swiss personal data transfers use safeguards such as EU Commission Model Contracts per the privacy policy.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: 256-bit encryption; SSL/TLS 1.2+ on API and application endpoints

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: AES-256 for data stored by Parabola, including production Customer Data

security.name: Hosting
security.value: Runs fully on AWS, servers in the United States, within a segregated VPC with firewalled subnets

security.name: Password storage
security.value: Never stored in plaintext; SHA-256 hashing derived from PBKDF2 with salts

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Annual independent third-party security assessments and penetration testing

security.name: Access control (Enterprise tier)
security.value: SSO & SAML, role-based access, usage analytics

security.name: Data handling in flows
security.value: Data passed through an automation flow is stored in memory and never written to disk; uploaded files are stored in secured Amazon S3 buckets

security.name: Subprocessors
security.value: Maintains a subprocessor list with 14 days' advance notice of changes to customers under DPA

products.name: Parabola (self-serve / team plans)
products.category: AI workflow automation for ops & finance
products.data_scope: Connects to and processes customer business data pulled from source systems (e.g. Shopify, NetSuite, ERP/3PL/warehouse systems) to build automated data flows
products.notes: Standard SOC 2 Type II, encryption, and DPA protections apply per the vendor's security page; no evidence of tier-gated security controls beyond SSO/SAML and role-based access.

products.name: Parabola Enterprise
products.data_scope: Same data scope as self-serve, plus dedicated automation-engineer implementation (8-12 week onboarding) and account-level access controls
products.notes: Adds SSO & SAML, role-based access, and usage analytics; enterprise page explicitly restates SOC 2 Type II as an included capability.

compare.data_residency: US (AWS-hosted); EU/Swiss transfers covered by contractual safeguards, no dedicated EU-region hosting documented

flags: A third-party aggregator (nudgesecurity.com) claims Parabola is ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR compliant. None of these claims are corroborated on parabola.io's own security, FAQ, DPA, or legal pages, and the vendor's own Terms/OMSA explicitly disclaim HIPAA Business Associate status and treat PCI and PHI data as 'Prohibited Data.'
A different, unrelated company, Parabol (parabol.co), a meeting and retrospective tool, has its own security FAQ page that could be confused with Parabola (parabola.io) in search results.

No formal hosted trust-center portal (e.g. Vanta/Drata/SafeBase Trust Center) was found; parabola.io/security is a self-authored security page, not an independently-hosted, continuously-updated trust portal.

AI-training no-train guarantee rests on vendor's own statement plus asserted DPAs with OpenAI and Anthropic; no opt-out control or tier distinction is documented for teams wanting to restrict AI steps entirely.
